translation.name: BSB
translation.licence_note: The Berean Standard Bible was dedicated to the public domain (CC0) on 30 April 2023. Attribution appreciated, not required.

note: What the book falls open at. The first reading is fixed: it is the one that puts the idea of welcoming a stranger into the Scribe's head, before any stranger exists to test it. Everything after is drawn at random. Themes match content/prints.json, so what the Scribe reads by day is what they are likely to cut at night. Verse text is fetched from the YouVersion Platform API by `make verses` and is not hand-entered; to add a reading, add the entry with an empty verse and rerun. A reference ending in `a` or `b` names half a verse, which the API does not do, so that excerpt is cut by hand and then preserved across reruns.

readings.verse: Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by so doing some people have entertained angels without knowing it.
readings.reflection:
Strangers. The word stops me. Every road I have walked, a stranger was the thing you watched the treeline for.

And here is a book, older than the ash, telling whoever finds it to feed one. To take one in. Whoever left this on that nightstand meant it to be found by somebody exactly as tired and exactly as frightened as I am.

I close it and sit with it a while.

readings.verse: For I was hungry and you gave Me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave Me something to drink, I was a stranger and you took Me in,
readings.reflection: Meat and drink and a door held open. Not a doctrine. A list of small ordinary things anybody could do, and most did not.

readings.verse: Isn’t it to share your bread with the hungry, to bring the poor and homeless into your home, to clothe the naked when you see him, and not to turn away from your own flesh and blood?
readings.reflection: That thou hide not thyself. I have hidden myself from people on a road before now, and told myself it was sense. Perhaps it was. It was still hiding.

readings.verse: You must treat the foreigner living among you as native-born and love him as yourself, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
readings.reflection: Because you were strangers yourselves. That is the whole of the argument, and I cannot get round it. I have been the one at the edge of somebody's firelight, being decided about.

readings.verse: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
readings.reflection: Not your friend. Your enemy. Whoever wrote this had met people, and wrote it anyway.

readings.verse: Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
readings.reflection: One another's. Both ways along the road. I have got very good at the carrying and very bad at the setting down.

readings.verse: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor. For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!
readings.reflection: Woe to him that is alone when he falleth. I read that line three times in the quiet of this room and then went and looked out of the window at nothing.

readings.verse: The Lord is near to the brokenhearted; He saves the contrite in spirit.
readings.reflection: Nigh. Near to. Not fixing it, not explaining it. Near to.

readings.verse: A bruised reed He will not break, and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish
readings.reflection: A wick still smoking is a wick that has gone out. And still nobody pinches it. I think about that longer than I mean to.
readings.note: Short opening excerpt, identified with the conventional 'a' suffix.

readings.verse: Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.
readings.reflection: Rest. I have not trusted a roof enough to sleep properly under one in four years. Tonight I might.

readings.verse: But those who wait upon the Lord will renew their strength; they will mount up with wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not faint.
readings.reflection: They shall walk, and not faint. Not fly. The walking is the part I know about.

readings.verse: But Ruth replied: “Do not urge me to leave you or to turn from following you. For wherever you go, I will go, and wherever you live, I will live; your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.
readings.reflection: Somebody said that to somebody. Out loud, to a person's face, on a road. That is a thing a person can decide to do.

readings.verse: The Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
readings.reflection: The dark does not understand the light and cannot argue with it either. A very small lamp is still a fact.

readings.verse: to console the mourners in Zion — to give them a crown of beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, and a garment of praise for a spirit of despair. So they will be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the Lord, that He may be glorified.
readings.reflection: Beauty for ashes. Written down long before the ash, by somebody who had no idea how literal they were being, and I am sitting in a valley that is trying to prove them right.

readings.verse: Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the sea. “Silence!” He commanded. “Be still!” And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm.
readings.reflection: Peace, be still. I know it is the sea he speaks to. I try the words on my own fear anyway. Quietly, so nobody can hear how badly I want them to work.

readings.verse: Today has enough trouble of its own.
readings.reflection: Sufficient unto the day. There is a plank loose over room two and rain due tonight. Tomorrow may have a hundred hungers in it, but this day has one plank.
readings.note: Short closing excerpt, identified with the conventional 'b' suffix.

readings.verse: At my first defense, no one stood with me, but everyone deserted me. May it not be charged against them.
readings.reflection: All men forsook me. The book does not pretend that good words keep people from leaving. The strange part is what comes after: he will not carry the leaving forward and lay it on them.

readings.verse: The Lord will watch over your coming and going, both now and forevermore.
readings.reflection: Going out and coming in. It makes a pair of them. I have always thought leaving was a door that shut behind you. This says a road may run both ways.

readings.verse: I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you.
readings.reflection: I do not know who speaks, or how a promise can cross so much dead time. I know what comfortless means without looking it up. I know what it would mean to see somebody coming.

readings.verse: But He said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.”
readings.reflection: Strength made perfect in weakness. Not after weakness is cured. In it. I have never heard anyone speak of the two as if they might inhabit the same body.
readings.note: Short opening excerpt, identified with the conventional 'a' suffix.

readings.verse: He lifted me up from the pit of despair, out of the miry clay; He set my feet upon a rock, and made my footsteps firm.
readings.reflection: Miry clay takes the shape of a road until your foot is in it. The part I keep is not the pit. It is feet on something that holds, and a way forward made steady.
